rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity — consolidates front-run check, module-to-module arc, Big Idea fidelity, and mood-doesn't-resolve-early into one verdict.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Front-run check: the lecture never names Ronacher's three-pattern or the practitioner attributions reserved for the closing lecture what-packaging-is.md, confirmed against the module's own 'Closing lecture pre-empt' push-back guard. Module-to-module arc: the lecture abstains from owning the M4->M5 or M5->M6 bridges (module file learn-from-the-test.md's 'Start here' and '## Next' sections carry those); the lecture's own close hands off to the exercise without claiming sequencing authority. Big Idea fidelity: module Big Idea is 'Read the un-packaged run through three failure-mode lenses, build the validation that would have caught each... The contrast is the lesson' (learn-from-the-test.md line 4) — the lecture leads with exactly this diagnostic-then-contrast framing and defers the build to the exercise. Mood doesn't resolve early: the lecture states the stance, the lenses, and one operational primitive, but withholds resolution — 'Hands-off option two' names three descriptive future artefacts without naming what they are, and 'Option two is what the exercise builds' explicitly defers the felt contrast to the exercise. One non-blocking drift found and logged as a TODO, not scored REVISE: content-strategy-agentic-engineering-101.md's M5-in-detail section (line 386) still describes this lecture as naming 'manual `/compact` at ~60%'; the body itself dropped that percentage on 2026-08-01 (per this file's own maintainer note: 'the 60% span it carried until 2026-08-01 went with the threshold', and the backing block's source-verification entries showing the figure was unbacked). The body correction is the right call — it removes an unsourced number — and the pedagogical shape the strategy doc actually cares about (one operational primitive, FAQ-only naming of the packaging trio) is unchanged. This is strategy-doc staleness, not an artefact defect.
